in situ resource utilization isru on titan broadly for any low tech survival strategy we have at a minimum six key survival needs on titan black inset box in the bottom left hand corner above and for our purposes here each of these is given an associated color clothing systems ie a spacesuit we can wear when we are outside lilac energy red shelter purple water blue food green oxygen cyan each resource label on the diagram above is then similarly designated with one or more of these associated colors to indicate the key survival need or needs which it might address 1 the sun resource label at number one fittingly on the diagram is the sun and this is given a red designation to indicate its role in meeting our energy needs yes the solar insolation level at the surface of titan is only a measly 015 of earth but even that relatively low level is still sufficient to be useful especially if it is concentrated by lenses or solar concentrators as is planned its certainly not something we should ignore 2 nitrogen and 3 methane resource labels 2 3 atmospheric nitrogen and methane respectively are both given a green designation for food production for nitrogen because its an essential source for organisms to fix into solid compounds and thus allow the growth of food plants and for methane because methanotrophic microorganisms directly metabolize methane into biomass and these will be one of our primary food generating organisms they dont need light or oxygen so are perfect for titan 4 hydrogen and 11 acetylene resource label 4 atmospheric hydrogen in combination with resource label 11 solid acetylene are both given a red color for energy as together they are the key components of a potentially very important energy producing chemical reaction namely the exothermic release of heat associated with the hydrogenation of acetylene atmospheric hydrogen or other free sources is preferred here as utilizing that represents a clear net positive production of energy rather than a net negative as would be the case for example if the required hydrogen was obtained by the electrolysis of water 5 wind power use of wind power on titan resource label 5 looks quite promising at 45x the density of earths atmosphere even a slow wind on titan carries a massive amount of kinetic energy a 5 ms breeze a light wind on titan may have the pushing power of a 22 ms gale on earth the situation is even better at higher altitudes which could be accessed by tethered balloons that would transmit electricity back to the ground via cable energy obtained in this manner is likely to be intermittent in nature yes but its too valuable a resource to ignore 6 tholinite and 7 water ice both resource label 6 exposed tholinite and resource label 7 exposed water ice have a purple designation due to their immense importance as structural material for buildings etc in fact these materials are likely to be the principal building materials on titan even beyond any low tech survival scenario as is being examined here tholinite is the compacted form of the looser and more powdery granular or tarry form of tholins typically found on the surface of titan in tholinite this loose form of tholin has fused under pressure into a substance similar to bituminous coal or hard asphalt though with the toughness of a very hard thermoplastic tholinite in appearance looks like a dark slightly plastic rock crucially this material can after minimal processing retain its tensile strength and structural integrity even at room temperatures 20c or 293k making it very suitable for the warm interiors of habitations eg for furniture inner walls etc water ice though in contrast is only suitable for the exteriors of structures where it retains its extraordinary strength in the very low temperatures typical of the titan environment layered or alternating walls using these materials separated by air gaps or vacuum in which ice is the outward facing component and tholinite the inward facing one would provide both excellent levels of insulation as well as being mechanically strong both these materials can be mined cut and shaped with only minimal technology making them extraordinarily valuable to humans on titan especially in any circumstances that preclude use of high technology additionally water ice has multiple other uses on titan too as it can be a source of drinking water be used in agriculture food production and after electrolysis be a readily available source of oxygen hence its further color designations of blue for water cyan for oxygen and green for food production 8 methane liquid based hydro electricity generation the case for including methane based hydro electric resource label number 8 as a source of energy for a titan colony is open to debate because the low gravity of titan 14 of earth combined with methanes much smaller mass in comparison to water means the output of a hydroelectric system is only a fraction of what it is on earth for example if we have a 10 meter drop of liquid at a flow rate of about 100 litres second a decent sized stream that will generate only 5 of the energy of the equivalent system on earth ie maybe approximately 185 watts not a lot however it has the advantage of being constant and running 247 unlike other more intermittent sources so as a background level of backup energy for a minimal set of essential systems its a good fit 9 clean tholins resource label 9 clean tholin is described as such to indicate its possible relatively pure character in the sense of it either being recently deposited on high ground and or not yet having been subjected to any additional lithificational hydrological like or methanological meteorological etc types of transformational processes it may therefore be particularly fluffy in which case it could serve as an excellent and astonishingly accessible insulating material potentially just needing to be scooped up of the ground of use both in habitation structures purple designation or as part of titan suitable protective attire lilac designation such loose tholin is given a further green color designation for food production because it is a prebiotic goldmine of substances useful to life and could also potentially serve as a structural framework for other organic materials which would then combine to form very fertile soils capable of supporting the growth of food plants and host other crucial soil based organisms from earth that are necessary for soil health whilst it is quite likely that a lot of food production in a titan colony will be done via advanced aeroponics and hydroponic systems it also make sense to have a fall back strategy not reliant on such complex artificial systems not as much anyway in case those systems fail at some point some pre processing and toxin removal from tholin tho will likely be required in order to achieve that but this could be relatively straightforward for example an initial phase of cyclic washingandbaking of the tholin followed by rinsing in warm water would dissolve and allow the removal of salts and the most dangerous watersoluble toxins like cyanides a period of heating would then follow which would drive off any remaining volatile organics and break the molecular bonds of the hydrophobic waxes making it wettable similar to earth soils at that point it could be inoculated with earth bacteria possibly from the titan colonists own body wastes these bacteria would then break down the complex tholin polymers into simple nitrates that the food plant roots could actually eat making the final produce very soil like in character 10 seas lakes and pools of liquid ethane and methane resource label 10 is for the hydrocarbons of the seas lakes and pools spread across the surface of titan particularly in the north this one is given a red designation ofcourse because of the capacity of their liquid components to release energy on oxidation though to be honest im not sure if that will be a net positive endeavour after the energy cost of water electrolysis to obtain the oxygen is factored in at any rate it will certainly be used as a compact form of relatively dense energy for gasoline driven vehicles of which there will eventually be a lot of on titan 11 solid acetylene evaporate see 4 above 12 cryominerals resource label 12 on the diagram shows various surface cryomineral cocrystal solids found scattered at various locations on the surface of titan that could serve a large variety of purposes the abundant acetyleneammonia cocrystal in particular resource label 12a could be of great importance as an energy source when suitably processed and is thus given a red color designation for potentially meeting some of a titan colonys energy needs suitable processing here could be its thermal dissociation into its two components the latter of which ammonia would be directed into a chamber containing a catalyst ironnickel mesh and then subject to heat causing its molecules to crack into hydrogen and nitrogen the hydrogen from this would then be directed into a chamber together with the acetylene which would react together exothermically also over a catalyst benzeneethane 12b and acrylonitrile 12c are both given lilac and purple color designations to indicate their potential role in the manufacture of clothing and buildings any released benzene from the benzeneethane cocrystal for example could be used in the manufacture of highstrength plastics acrylonitrile cocrystals these are the holy grail for materials acrylonitrile for example can be polymerized into carbon fiber and highgrade acrylics having it in a cocrystal form makes it much easier to purify 13 meteorite fragments subsurface ejecta resource label 13 heavier elements and metals etc are far rarer on titan then they are on earth and one of the only handful of places where we could reasonably expect to find them is at the site of meteorite impacts there are two reasons for this the first is that the ejecta of such impacts contain subsurface material and since titan is only partly geologically differentiated its possible these will contain heavier elements the second reason is more direct the meteorite itself could contain heavier elements and depending on whether or not it fragmented on impact these would then be found at one or more locations within the impact site whilst neither iron resource label 13a nor nickel resource label 13b are a direct source of energy theyve both been given a red for energy designation anyway because they can be an essential component in the production of energy which is just as important eg as a catalyst for the hydrogenation of acetylene iron in addition is given a further purple color designation because of its likely use in the creation of specialised components of shelter habitation structures though the vast quantity of materials used there will be tholins tholinderivatives plastics or water ice silicate rocks could also be present in the impact site if these were part of the ejecta or meteorite body these could meet our needs for shelter where the rocks could form part of the external structure of buildings or after grinding and processing as a constituent part of artificial soils in order to aid plant growth these resources hence are given a green and purple color designation 14 geothermal whilst the geothermal energy gradient seems negligible at most locations on titans surface within its most superficial layer say down to 50 meters or so there are potentially active cryovolcanic sites such as doom mons or sotra patera where this could be far more pronounced the immediate subsurface near those sites could be a slushy mixture of liquid water and ammonia at temperatures as high as roughly 90c 179k or higher compared to the surface at temperature of 179c 94k this is a staggering temperature differential which could be readily exploited for energy generation needs thus this potential resource is given a red color designation for potentially meeting our energy needs in fact it is not beyond the bounds of possibility that in some regions those higher subsurface temperatures could be far closer to the actual surface potentially creating astonishingly earth like conditions where a person could somewhat comfortably walk around wearing only standard earth clothing and a simple oxygen mask all other considerations aside such places or areas near to such places therefore are clear candidates for a human colony site 15 volcanic ejecta brine flows resource label 15 is volcanic ejecta brine flows at formerly or currently active cryovolcanic sites one potentially very serious material deficit we may find on titan is the lack of some trace mineral nutrients resource item 15a that are absolutely essential for human health some examples of these are potassium k sodium na phosphorus p calcium ca and in particular iodine i and selenium se which appear to be completely absent at the surface in general the only reasonable locations these could be found in adequate quantities is within current or past brine salt flow areas associated with active cryovolcanism this is because such flows ultimately originate from titans internal ocean which is likely a concentrated brine solution containing significant quantities of trace elements that have leached out from the silicate core resource label 15b is silicates rocks and described here for the same reasons given in item 13 above 15 dissolved noble gases there is a dearth of noble gasses in titans atmosphere and its possible this is so because they are dissolved in its liquid methane and ethane seas and lakes etc instead if that is the case these could be mined via for example pumping and processing operations allowing a potential colony on titan to gain access to them noble gasses are incredibly useful with applications ranging from welding and metallurgy where argon can prevent the formation of brittle nitrides and fire suppression within habitats where such inert gasses can rapidly prevent the spread of fire to thermal insulation functions of buildings where if confined between any external doublewalls they can prevent heat loss far more capably than titans standard nitrogenrich atmosphere it is for those reasons therefore that this resource is given a purple color designation for its potential role in contributing to our need for strong and safe shelter

advise needed for where to focus my spare money in the past i have always spent everything i earnt personally and now i have reduced my outgoings significantly im not sure what to do with the extra money for the last six months ive spent too much on holidays and meals out and other useless things that will not benefit me in older age i could really do with some advice that is practical as i think the flow chart doesnt exactly fit my situation i own a ltd company that has over 1m on the balance sheet so i have never really worried about ahving savings if the worst happened and i needed money i could pay myself a lump sum and just pay the tax me and my wife both take 100k each a month through a mix of salary and dividends the company also pays my pension contributuions currently i have 220k in my director opension and 50k in a pot from a prevoious job i am in the process of merging the two my planned contributuion is 20k more before the end of this tax year and not sure for next year my wifes only pension is what she gets from her salary with the business which is probably minimal 8 years with nest i have an electric company car and phone is covered through work monthly numbers income after tax 11100 mortgage 2717 with a year left to go on fixed rate utilites that i pay 832 mclaren finance 842 considering selling as i dont use it no debt except the mortgage 20k in a normal savings account not isa my car insurance is about 3k due in march and i usually pay that in a lump amount i have a share in a small airplane which is worth around 20k im trying to sell as i dont fly it but that may be a long process as its quite specialist not sure if it matters but we have two children 16 and 11 years old my wife pays a small amount of the bills and the usual parent costs for school and clubs etc which arent included above and she has her own spending money i pay for our holidays meals out and anything else that comes up my thoughts are that it seems pointless to have more savings as i can access the companies money if needed the money is also better in the business as we have a lot of debt stocking plans for vehicles that we sell although the accountant says we dont need to worry about reducing it i would still like to do that for peace of mind so i dont want to pay myself anymore the business is profitable and will reduce the debt by 200k a year maybe more so i think my only options are overpay on my mortgage or reduce my wages and get the company to pay extra into my pension any helpadvice really would be greatly appreciated on any positive changes i could make

closing the hazard awareness delay realtime grid visibility with active grid response utility safety podcast by incident prevention magazine in this episode of incident preventions utility safety podcast host kate wade sits down with tim bedford a 36year veteran of pge and current principal customer success manager at gridware together they explore a critical new category of grid intelligence active grid response tim explains the concept of hazard awareness delaythe dangerous gap in time between a grid event occurring and the utility becoming aware of it by utilizing gridwares gridscope a mechanical sensing device installed on poles utilities can now detect hazards like broken poles vegetation impact and conductor vibration in realtime listen in to learn how realtime grid visibility eliminates unnecessary exposure for linemen drastically improving utility safety the role of mechanical sensing in preventing wildfires by identifying risks before they ignite how gridwares technology creates a zero delay line break response potentially deenergizing falling lines before they hit the ground strategies for funding safety technology through reliability and fleet maintenance budgets whether you are in operations safety management or fleet logistics this episode offers actionable insights into modernizing grid protection guest contact tim bedford timbedfordgridwareiomailtotimbedfordgridwareio learn more wwwgridwareio key takeaways defining hazard awareness delay this is the critical time lapse between an event occurring on the electrical system and the utilitys awareness of it reducing this delay prevents outages and catastrophic events like wildfires mechanical sensing technology gridwares gridscope acts like a pickup on a guitar string detecting vibration sound and pole angle changes to pinpoint exact fault locations without needing to patrol the entire line enhancing lineman safety by providing the exact location of a fault utilities reduce the need for linemen to patrol hazardous terrain in the dark significantly lowering safety risks and exposure rapid installation the devices are approximately the size of a shoebox weigh 35 lbs and can be installed in under five minutes a single crew can install upwards of 50 devices per day future zero delay capabilities gridware is currently piloting technology that can detect a line break and trigger a recloser to deenergize the circuit before the wire even hits the ground qa utility safety grid visibility q what is the active grid response solution provided by gridware a active grid response is a new category of grid intelligence that provides realtime visibility into the physical electrical and environmental conditions of the grid it uses sensors to monitor vibrations and pole angles allowing utilities to identify specific hazardslike a tree striking a line or a car hitting a polebefore they escalate into major outages or wildfires q how does this technology directly improve utility safety for the workforce a it drastically reduces the hunt and seek method of finding faults instead of a troubleman patrolling miles of line in hazardous conditions darkness rough terrain severe weather the system provides a pinpoint location this minimizes the time employees spend in dangerous environments and reduces fleet vehicle exposure q is this technology costprohibitive for smaller utilities or tight budgets a tim bedford suggests that funding often comes from shifting budgets based on the use case for example the technology offsets costs in fleet fuel engine hours and patrol time additionally it can replace less effective legacy devices like standard fault indicators and deployments can be scaled to focus only on highrisk protection zones rather than the entire system immediately subscribe to incident prevention magazine register for the ip utility safety conference expo utilitysafety gridmodernization linemansafety im overjoyed i dont expect this post to get much traffic but im so happy right now i had to share my experience i bought my 4xe grand cherokee maybe two years ago used with less than 5000 miles and everything was great then after a battery recall everything started falling apart one issue after another the charging light on the dashboard stopped working the heat wouldnt turn on half the time the parking assist wouldnt be available at times android auto would be muted the vehicle literally shut off once the active lane management tried to drive me off the road once sometines electric mode wouldnt be available or hybrid mode wouldnt use the battery at all there was a coolant leak that came out of nowhere there were other minor issues that i wont bother to mention i treated the vehicle very well and mostly only ever drive it to work or date nights i never sped and always kept it serviced so i dont know why it had so many issues the vehicle was always driveabie but all of these issues made me begin to resent my purchase anyway i had to go to the dealership for the latest battery recall and decided i to mention all of the issues i was having they kept my vehicle for four days even though it was supposed to be a three hour job in the meantime the customer service rep gave me a brand new 80k vehicle with less than 100 miles on it to drive around in as a loaner which made no sense to me but i wasnt going to turn them down and when it was time for the bill it was an astounding 000 they told me that everything was still covered with the warranty the customer service was so nice the jeep feels like it just drove off of the assembly line everything works flawlessly maybe its the bare minimum and they were just making things right i dont know what i do know is this almost every vehicle ive purchased since 2007 has been a grand cherokee i even bought my wife a grand cherokee i was beginning to have second thoughts about my loyalty but now i dont i love my dealership and my faith in the brand is reaffirmed they have a loyal customer for life

immigrating to australia a true story so i figured i would do a post of immigrating to australia as a police officer from the uk in the hopes it gives someone some clarity if it is for them this will be a fairly long post as i am going to try to cover everything that may be a question to someone somewhere i will break it down into topics to also make it easier to read as some parts wont be interesting to people i will also refer to everything in dollars and not sterling so half the value and that gives you sterling background pre immigration i was a cop in southeast england for around 7 years all that time was frontline with a little side gig with mast acting sgt and various other skills i have a wife with 2 very young children 2 and 5 at the time of coming over my wife and i have always wanted to migrate to australia however we had some issues which we thought would prevent us ill get to that further down we have no family and friends in australia prior to migrating and did not know anyone that had done this i learnt this all just by going through the process queensland police recruitment come 2023 i see a post on reddit and a comment under that post about queensland police recruiting i was against applying to wa due to its isolation to the rest of the country so seeing this comment whoever you are changed the course of my life i looked into the queensland police qps international recruitment page and digested all their information and decided it was worth a crack the recruitment process was long and drawn out taking roughly a year from my email of expression to getting an official offer the recruitment process may have changed but essentially they sent out some forms and activities to complete such as medical fitness tests etc in sections and there would be long waits of about a month between each stage to find out what the next stage was interview and some other tests had to be done at night due to the time zone difference part of the process was asking for my skill set which i believe indicated the pay point i would start in qps the more skills and rank the higher the pay point due to my skills and active sgt exam i achieved a higher pay point the recruitment stage was a bit drawn out and frustrating due to the amount of time it took however the qps were willing to sponsor my visa if i were successful through the checks so it seemed they were doing their due diligence before they spent money after i passed all the stages i was offered a position within the qps as a frontline officer you have to start here regardless of your rank or skills which they call general duties i was allowed to nominate 3 areas of preference i would want to be deployed and i achieved my second choice once this all went through the qps sent me some documents to start the visa process at this point i would say i was at month 10 into process visa medical my wife was very adamant we would not qualify for the visa which was a 186 visa the best one you can get as it gives full residence full medical schools etc and had a timeframe of 6 weeks from application to result this is one below becoming a citizen this is because she has a longstanding illness kidney transplant and required daily medication for the rest of her life we looked into this on the australian immigration website to get some clarity but it was a little wishy washy with a concrete answer essentially the website stated that anyone requiring an organ transplant or dialysis would be denied a visa as these procedures have a shortage in australia hence why my wife was very skeptical of gaining a visa although she was no longer on dialysis and did not need a transplant she most definitely will in the future we also looked into the cost of getting her medication privately as australian visa state that any medical cost exceeding 50k over 10 years would be not worth the risk well guess what thats how much my wifes medication would cost but despite her certainty we were not going to make it we decided to entertain the idea because we would always regret it if we didnt try but there were further issues the medical aspect was at the very end of the visa application and you have to fork up the full cost of the visa before you are given the nod that you are successful or not so between myself my wife and two children the visa was 10k and we could still be told no we completed all the paperwork the police checks etc that all went through and then we were sent the forms for the medical and had to attend a dedicated medical facility in london others nationwide are available so we decided to make a day out in london and do the medical early doors that cost more money i think another 1k we were literally haemorrhaging money at this point and could still be told no by the australian immigrations office we did our medical which took about 45 minutes you get your medical report a few days later but have to request it otherwise the facility will just automatically send it to the immigration office during the medical both my wife and i had separate doctors assessing us and we both stated her history and what our chances were well both doctors have differing opinions with one stating it shouldnt be a problem and the other stating we were wasting our time when we received the medical report our children had glowing reports while mine and my wifes was not they grade it either a or b a being ok b being not ok both my wife and i got b i received this because i donated the kidney to my wife and so was deemed at risk which is mad because i am actually more healthy then the average joe so reading these reports we figured our dream was dead and we should just move on with our lives the immigration office had the reports but had not made a decision yet on if our application was successful after a couple of weeks i finally heard back via email from the immigration office and we were all successful what a feeling we all had preparing to move so from receiving that visa we had 8 weeks until my start date for my new job with the qps i handed my notice in straight away and did not return the following day as i had so much leave built up my sgt told me not to return we owned our house so had to start straight away selling it on the market within the week offer the following week the rest of the sale occurred while we were in australia but had no hiccups we decided we would only ship 6 boxes via ship to australia and sell everything else to save money to transport costs learn from me here as this was a mistake we should have shipped more as we find ourselves missing some things we either sold threw away or left behind my advice would be to take anything sentimental small items and expensive things furniture and electricals leave behind as it isnt worth it we met people who brought stuff over on a container and found it was too expensive a headache and doesnt fit with the climate plus the stuff on a container took almost 6 months and most furniture had to be purchased again anyway i spent the rest of my time off selling everything we had said our goodbyes to family and jetted off giving me only 12 days from landing in australian to starting my new job accommodation this was a difficult one to manage so in qld the estate agents will not lease you a property unless you physically inspect it yourself or an agent some people pay money to a third party to secure them accommodation save yourself that money as it can be and do a little groundwork yourself i used realestatecomau or domaincomau and found plenty of rentals you cant be picky so i emailed several of them with most turning me down due to being out of the country however i found a couple of real estate agents who would give me a shot and i secured the property by signing a contract and sending the deposit they say there is a property crisis here but thats for very affordable housing i found looking for something a little more expensive was far easier finding a 4 bed property was easy as they are in abundance in qld between landing and getting my rental as it would be void of any furniture i hired an airbnb for the 12 days giving me ample time to get everything we need to furnish a house my wife very much enjoyed spending the money from everything we sold in the uk houses here are far bigger then in the uk they are more expensive but you are getting more for that money if you get a new build you do not get much garden as plots of land prices are expensive here finances right so you need money a lot honestly i found having savings took the financial burden off us that would have caused difficulties and perhaps regret of making the move i would say as a family we spent 60k in our first few weeks that was all our savings over a decade gone in 3 weeks but this secured us our accommodation deposit on accommodation furniture two vehicles and some fun stuff we choose to buy 2 second hand cars outright because we had no credit score here some people i know secured a loan car we used wisecom to transfer all of our money from the uk to aus dollars as they provided the best rate with a small fee we banked with hsbc in the uk and found that they also have a branch in qld some popping into a branch in the uk allowed me to open a qld account looking back if we arrived with very little money i dont know how we would have managed immigration is hard enough without worrying about how to afford things so i would say if you have less then 20k it is going to be hard especially for a family after landing you must apply for a tax reference number trn it is free through the gov website so do not be conned by third party sites you will also need to visit a place called centrelink in qld if you have kids so you can claim government subsidy on childcare they will also set you up with an account so you can use over government services such as tax services and their version of the nhs medicare food is much more expensive here eat seasonal for example at the moment a bag of apples say 6 is 8 because they are not seasonal they are usually half the price energy is cheaper than the uk by almost half fuel is so much cheaper again almost half eating out is a bit cheaper there are loads of free stuff to do for kids such as pools play equipment splash parks they even do free electric bbqs in all local parks family so after landing securing a school for my 5yearold was simple however bring their identity documents in your suitcase not shipped they need to sight the original birth certificate he started school the same time i started work getting a daycare for my daughter was a bit harder same in the uk there isnt enough spaces we put her on a waiting list and she started her daycare 4 months later my wife took this opportunity to not work just yet and spend the time with our daughter again this is why it is a good idea to be financially stable when arriving this took pressure off my wife having to find work so quickly daycare here is more expensive than the uk by a little bit but it is subsidized by the government you must apply for this speak to centrelink and they can set this up qld love apps so there is an app for centrelink and you can do it all from your phone honestly i struggled a bit so just went to see them in person they have offices everywhere the job so is the job better here that is personal opinion i loved my old role my old team and my old life in the uk i didnt leave on bad terms i had career aspirations and promotion on the horizon but gave it all up for a life here in my opinion the job can be shit anywhere in the world were we police they all have their own issues their odd way of doing things and some things they do right qps is no different if you are considering leaving uk policing to come to qps because you think it will be better then i highly suggest you do some further research i do not think the qps is better than my previous jurisdiction there is vastly more paperwork here they over record incidents and are extremely risk adverse they train you at their academy for 4 months an external recruit is 9 months to which it is mostly legislation reports and learning their computer systems if you use new niche thats what they use here but far deeper there practical skills are not the same as the uk i cannot delve too much but the courses in the uk are longer and you can instantly see why cops in the uk are trained to a higher standard for driving pursuits and physical skills cops in australia are armed so this is a new skill to learn you are called a first year constable for a year once you leave the academy this fosters a culture of elitism as you are not allowed to leave the station alone are not allowed to patrol alone and are expected to do all the dirty work regardless of previous experience it has been one of the hardest working years of my policing life sometimes i have even considered leaving the job as it really does grind you down in my intake alone of 50 experience officers from around the world 6 have quit and looked for work elsewhere some even returning to their home countries so again dont come here thinking the work is better it is not it is different it is all about how we adapt to it and overcome the differences there are some positives every officer is double crewed this is both for safety tactics as well as splitting the load when it comes to filling out paperwork the officer decides to charge offenders based on evidence not a sgt or prosecutions all overtime is double time and no losing 30 minutes and if you do overtime on a bank holiday it is quad time a cop here can earn a lot of money with overtime i mean a lot of money there are many more positives and negatives medical so qld version of nhs is called medicare with the 186 visa we gain access to this it is similar to the nhs however there are some financial hits you have to pay to see the gp costs about 25 but the plus side to this is that you can usually see the gp that same day or the next no waiting 4 weeks anymore emergency care is free and so in the ambulance some other states in australia charge you for an ambulance my wife has had a few medical complications since arriving she has a consultant for the kidney stuff just like the uk they do keep on top of it here some procedures cost money but then are reimbursed back through medicare i would say it is just as good as the nhs not better or worse prescriptions are a little more expensive too weather and animals it gets hot here and muggy in summer if you dont like heat you will struggle but a lot of places are air conditioned like the shopping centres everything is designed to manage the heat i dont mind the heat sometimes you are stuck on the motorway in the blazing sun so carry water sunscreen and a hat deadly animals everywhere they say bullshit ive seen a few spiders in more rural properties and not a single wild spider in the 18 months i have been here cockroaches in the house are far more common but are easy to get rid of and you get used to them so if the creepy crawlies are putting you off then go more urban then rural it is barely noticeable conclusion best decision me and my wife ever made the kids are thriving as we do so much outdoors loads of water play eating out is geared towards families as well as most have play areas of activities for kids which are free there have been difficult times when we look back at what we had with our careers and life in the uk but the hard work here is paying off and we are reaping the benefits it is more expensive to live here but we get paid more doing the same job im on the equivalent of an insp wage if anyone has more questions that i have not covered please comment so i can answer it openly for other people if you have that question chances are someone else does i will absolutely help out where i can

trump launches project vault a 12 billion minerals stockpile to counter china president donald trump is poised to unveil a major new strategic initiative known as project vault a massive 12 billion undertaking designed to shield american manufacturers from supply chain shocks and reduce the nations heavy reliance on chinese materials this venture seeks to create a criticalminerals stockpile specifically for the private sector functioning similarly to the nations emergency oil reserve but focused entirely on the raw materials that power modern technology and industry the initiative addresses a glaring vulnerability in the united states industrial base a deep dependence on china for rare earths and other metals china currently dominates the global processing of these elements which are vital components for products ranging from electric vehicle batteries and jet engines to smartphones following beijings recent tightening of export controls the administration is moving to insulate us companies from geopolitical leverage and potential price volatility project vault is structured as a significant publicprivate partnership it combines a recordsetting 10 billion loan from the us exportimport bankmore than double the banks nextlargest dealwith 167 billion in private capital while the us already maintains a stockpile for defense needs this represents the first stockpile specifically designed to support the civilian industrial economy the exportimport banks board is scheduled to authorize the 15year loan on monday coinciding with a highprofile meeting between president trump gm ceo mary barra and mining magnate robert friedland to finalize the effort the project has already attracted participation from over a dozen major corporations across the automotive aerospace and technology sectors the roster of industry titans committed to the project includes general motors co stellantis nv boeing co alphabet incs google ge vernova inc and corning inc to facilitate the physical acquisition of these materials three major commodities trading houseshartree partners lp traxys north america llc and mercuria energy group ltdhave been enlisted to handle the complex logistics of procurement under the agreement participating manufacturers will pay carrying costs and upfront fees to reserve materials in the event of a major supply disruption these companies will have guaranteed access to the stockpile additionally the program includes a mechanism where companies commit to repurchasing materials at set prices a strategy designed to suppress the massive price swings that can wreak havoc on corporate balance sheets

energy news latest sustainability news pioneering advancements in battery technology in todays fastpaced world sustainability has become more than just a buzzword it is an urgent imperative demanding attention and innovation from industries worldwide one area making considerable strides toward sustainability is battery technology from luxury electric vehicles to groundbreaking research recent developments have underscored the sustainable future were heading towards heres a look at the latest sustainability news focusing on battery advancements porsches cayenne electric a leap in luxury evs revolutionizing electric vehicles with doublesided cooling this week porsche made headlines by launching the cayenne electric an allelectric version of its popular suv this isnt just any electric vehicle its set to redefine luxury ev standards with its avantgarde 113 kwh highvoltage battery a standout feature is the worldfirst doublesided cooling technology bringing more efficient and effective thermal management to ev batteries than ever before source cooling is pivotal in maximizing battery performance and lifespan traditionally batteries are cooled from one side which can lead to uneven temperature distribution and inefficient energy use by cooling from both above and below porsches new system ensures a balanced temperature profile optimizing the batterys performance and potentially extending its life this innovative approach allows the cayenne electric to boast an impressive range of over 600 kilometers and supports 800volt fast charging setting a new benchmark for performance and efficiency in electric vehicles impact on sustainable transportation porsches launch is significant for the luxury car segment demonstrating that sustainability and luxury can coexist without compromise the cayenne electric represents a critical step towards reducing the carbon footprint of luxury vehicles while maintaining the high performance expected by discerning customers this innovation signifies a broader shift in the automotive industry towards embracing sustainable practices and technologies catls ultrafast charging battery balancing speed and longevity durability meets speed in battery technology in another remarkable development contemporary amperex technology co limited catl announced a breakthrough in ultrafast charging battery technology their new 5c battery is engineered to endure an astonishing 18 million kilometers even under rapid charging conditions source this advancement addresses a prevalent challenge in electric vehicle adoption the tradeoff between charging speed and battery longevity ultrafast charging typically puts substantial stress on batteries often reducing their lifespan catls innovation signifies a step forward demonstrating that its possible to provide speed without sacrificing the durability of the battery future implications for electric vehicles this breakthrough is crucial for the sustainability of electric vehicles making them more practical and appealing for consumers transitioning from traditional fuelpowered cars by enhancing the batterys resilience and charging speed catl is helping alleviate range anxiety and promoting faster more widespread adoption of electric vehicles solidstate battery breakthroughs the future is solid chinese researchers unveil breathable silicon anode further pushing the envelope in battery technology chinese researchers have unveiled a breathable silicon anode for solidstate batteries this represents a crucial development in the path toward commercializing nextgeneration solidstate batteries source solidstate batteries offer significant benefits over conventional lithiumion batteries including higher energy density improved safety and longer lifespan however challenges in finding suitable materials for the anodes have impeded their broader adoption the introduction of a breathable silicon anode marks a critical step in overcoming these barriers unleashing the potential of solidstate batteries solidstate batteries are seen as the holy grail for energy storage with the potential to transform electric vehicles and renewable energy sectors as research continues breakthroughs like these bring us closer to realizing their full potential promising safer more efficient power storage solutions that could revolutionize multiple industries conclusion the road to a sustainable future the recent advancements in battery technology are not just technological feats they are pivotal steps toward a sustainable future as companies like porsche and catl push boundaries they set new standards for industries worldwide challenging others to innovate and adopt more sustainable practices the journey towards sustainability is a collective effort where each breakthrough no matter how small contributes to the larger goal of preserving our environment for future generations as these technologies evolve we can look forward to a world that not only demands less from our planet but also provides more reliable efficient and sustainable solutions stay tuned as the race to innovate for sustainability continues driving us toward a greener future with each new development

twin cities rapid transit car 1300 operating on the grounds of the minnesota streetcar museum minneapolis mn 2023 on a rainy day in 2023 we had to park under a bridge so this historic wooden streetcar wouldnt be damaged by a sudden burst of heavy rain it is one of few remaining wooden streetcars that was always a streetcar never converted to something else the second rebuild completed in november 1931 left us with approximately what you see today the major modification in 1931 was to allow for 2man operation the original coal stove for heat in these frigid minnesota winters was removed on a prior rebuild and replaced by electric heaters powered by the overhead 600 volts dc power all the electronics in the car including the lights were originally powered directly by 600 volts dc technical info built 1908 st paul minnesota refurbished 1928 1931 retired 1954 system dismantled fate on retirement donated to the minnesota railfans association in 1954 trucks 2 baldwin 5 traction power 2 ge 213 motors power type overhead single wire 600 volts dc vehicle weight empty 47800 lbs modern inservice date 1971 modern system minnesota streetcar museum as a museumeducational piece

warning strike starting at 300 am the action halts most bvg subways and buses though deutsche bahns sbahn and regional trains remain unaffected while passengers are barred from boarding the bvg will operate empty trams to prevent overhead lines from freezing rbb24 this unusual measure of running ghost trams follows a recent service collapse caused by ice rain which froze power lines for days to from home to avoid expected gridlock spiegel verdi is escalating pressure ahead of tuesdays negotiations demanding improved working conditions rather than just higher wages specific requests include a ruled on wednesday that tenants are forbidden from making a profit through subletting the court clarified that while subletting is a legitimate way to cover rent while away it cannot be turned into a business model any income exceeding actual housing expenses is now considered a violation of the primary rental agreement rbb24 the ruling stemmed from a berlin case where a tenant charged 962 for a flat with a base rent of 460 though the tenant claimed the surcharge was for extensive furnishings like a dishwasher and sound system the court upheld the landlords eviction notice this sets a intelligence reports indicate politically motivated leftwing crime rose 38 in 2024 us news world report this historic financial incentive underlines the severity of infrastructure vulnerabilities as what is bldc bldc is an acronym for brushless direct current bldc is a motor technology that operates on direct current dc and does not have brushes inside the motor since there are no brushes the motor is smoother cooler and less wasteful of electricity in simple terms bldc is a more intelligent and efficient motor technology than the traditional motor technology bldc motors have an electronic controller for speed and power control unlike traditional motors that have physical contact components this makes bldc motors more reliable longerlasting and energyefficient bldc technology is currently used in ceiling fans electric vehicles air conditioners washing machines computer cooling systems bldc technology is primarily recognized for its powersaving noiseless and longerlasting properties than traditional motor technology

kia k4 sportswagon ev5 gt and ev2 not coming to australia kia australia has cooled expectations around several highprofile models confirming the k4 sportswagon ev5 gt and ev2 are all unlikely to reach local showrooms due to emissions regulations pricing pressure and sourcing complexity k4 sportswagon fails nves test the recently revealed kia k4 sportswagon will not be offered in australia with kia citing the federal governments new vehicle efficiency standard nves as the main barrier kia australia says lowvolume combustion or hybrid wagons generate far fewer emissions credits than electric vehicles making them difficult to justify under the nves framework even a future fullhybrid version of the k4 is unlikely to change the equation from 2027 onwards while wagons retain popularity in europe demand continues to shrink locally with only a handful of mainstream models still offered in australia ev5 gt blocked by sourcing and cost the ev5 gt unveiled earlier this year has also been ruled out although the ev5 range sold in australia is sourced from china the gt variant is built in south korea creating cost and logistics complications kia australia says importing the koreanbuilt model would push pricing well beyond the current ev5 range undermining its value positioning this is despite the ev5 gt offering similar straightline performance to the locally sold ev5 awd long range albeit with sportier hardware and chassis tuning with the ev6 gt already on sale and the ev9 gt due later this year kia sees little need for another niche performance ev ev2 unlikely to meet price expectations at the entry level kia has poured cold water on the ev2 its smallest electric suv built in slovakia the ev2 faces higher production and shipping costs making it difficult to price comfortably below the ev3 which starts from 47600 plus onroad costs in australia kia has acknowledged growing pressure from lowcost chinese evs such as the byd atto 1 and gwm ora which are setting increasingly aggressive benchmarks for affordable electric vehicles in the local market

be extra careful before performing a diy project be extra careful before performing a diy project because you can do more harm than good i did what i thought was a simple and easy diy project on my dodge charger and i ended up doing more harm than good i knew it was time to change out my headlights since the current lights were showing signs of getting old as they were omitting a yellowish amber type colored light i purchased the 6000k led lights from my local oreillys i installed them and waited until it was dark so i could test them out they were not as bright as i wanted them to be when i did followup research i found out that the little led chips that were on the sides of the housing unit research indicated that the led chips needed to be inserted left to right or 3pm to 9pm according to a clocks standard so i reinserted them correctly and checked them out in the dark and they looked good the very next morning i tried to start my car and it wouldnt start this is because i did not lock the leds in place by turning the entire headlight unit either right or left to lock them into place i contacted the dodge dealerships service dept and they informed me that its never a good idea to install led lights into a dodge charger they need their original type housing units and plug in type units opposed to the aftermarket ones that do not look like the original ones so i went back to oreillys and purchased the original halogens at their brightest form i could find and installation was way easier especially clicking them into place plus with the halogen units you can turn them however you want because they have the simple bulb like feature to where you dont need to insert them a certain way in conclusion i had to jump my car battery since it wouldnt turn over just because the initial leds were not locked into place i did more research and come to find out dodge chargers are super sensitive when it comes to just changing out the headlights this can cause a huge negative shift in your electrical side of things right down to the vehicle not being able to start also if your about to perform a diy project make sure your able to perform a reverse method of what you took apart before putting things back together in the original manner in which you took something apart

preorder reservations a metric for startup success or merely a mirror of mainstream consumer trends ive been looking to purchase my second ev specifically i want a small pickup truck when the telo was announced i immediately put down a 152 reservation likewise when the slate was announced i immediately put down a 100 deposit since my first ev purchase didnt turn out so well my unconventional urban runabout an arcimoto fuv suddenly failed after three years of enjoyable use much like the parent company so ive been looking for tells that might help me avoid another money pit since ai is all the rage i decided to ask google ai a simple question how many preorder reservations do these companies actually have q how many telo truck reservations are there a as of early 2026 telo trucks has reported over 12000 reservations for its mt1 compact electric pickup the company saw a significant surge in interest throughout 2025 for context they had roughly 3700 reservations in late 2024 and hit the 5000 mark in march 2025 by the time they secured their 20 million series a funding round in september 2025 the number had jumped to 12000 representing over 600 million in potential revenue q how many slate truck reservations are there a as of early 2026 the slate truck the affordable minimalist ev pickup from slate auto has reached over 100000 reservations the company achieved this milestone in may 2025 just a few weeks after opening its reservation system this is particularly notable given that the slate truck is positioned as a practical alternative to the cybertruck featuring a 20000 starting price and a utilitarian design basically having put down hard earned cash on a three wheel ev classified as a motorcycle also asked q how many aptera reservations are there a as of early 2026 aptera motors has approximately 49000 reservations for its solar electric vehicle this number has grown steadily since the companys revival though it is important to distinguish between general reservations and the accelerator program which represents the customers at the very front of the line and by way of comparison asked q how many preorder reservations did arcimoto have before it failed a while arcimoto did not release a final precise preorder count immediately before its operations ceased in 2024 its official filings and historical reports provide a clear picture of the numbers it reached at its peak and where they stood during its decline at its height arcimoto claimed over 5000 preorders but this number was heavily scrutinized by investors and analysts due to high refund rates and stale leads bottom line asking ai about the number of reservations ive got the feeling that slate has the better chance of finding market success than telo thoughts

cobalt and battery materials cobalt a vital component in advanced battery technologies cobalt co is a transition metal widely valued for its critical role in modern rechargeable battery materials it is particularly important in lithiumion battery cathodes where it helps deliver high energy density long cycle life and reliable electrochemical performance these characteristics make cobaltcontaining materials essential for applications ranging from consumer electronics to electric vehicles and largescale energy storage systems electrochemical stability and performance cobaltbased cathode materials exhibit excellent electrochemical stability enabling batteries to operate at higher voltages while maintaining consistent capacity over repeated chargedischarge cycles by stabilizing the layered crystal structure of cathode materials cobalt helps reduce degradation and improves overall battery efficiency this makes cobalt especially valuable in highperformance batteries that require both power and durability high energy density and long cycle life the presence of cobalt in battery cathodes contributes significantly to high energy density allowing more energy to be stored in a compact and lightweight form cobalt also enhances cycle life by reducing structural fatigue during repeated lithium insertion and extraction as a result batteries with cobaltcontaining materials support longer operating times and extended service life in demanding applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics thermal stability and safety cobalt plays an important role in improving the thermal stability of battery materials it helps maintain structural integrity at elevated temperatures and reduces the risk of thermal runaway these safetyrelated benefits are critical for batteries used in automotive aerospace and industrial energy storage applications where reliability under stress is essential role in advanced battery chemistries cobalt is a key component in widely used cathode chemistries such as lithium cobalt oxide lco lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide nmc and lithium nickel cobalt aluminum oxide nca these materials are engineered to balance energy density power output and safety ongoing research aims to optimize cobalt content to improve performance while reducing material costs and supply risks key applications of cobalt in battery materials cobalts unique combination of electrochemical performance thermal stability and structural support makes it indispensable in advanced energy storage technologies including lithiumion batteries for smartphones laptops and consumer electronics electric vehicle batteries requiring high energy density and long service life gridscale energy storage systems supporting renewable energy integration highreliability batteries for aerospace and industrial power systems as global demand for electrification and energy storage continues to grow cobalt remains a cornerstone material in advanced battery technologies continued innovation in battery design recycling and alternative chemistries will shape how cobalt is used ensuring high performance while addressing sustainability and supplychain there alternatives to cobalt in batteries yes chemistries like lfp and highnickel cathodes reduce or eliminate cobalt though often with tradeoffs in energy density or performance q3 is cobalt supply a concern cobalt sourcing faces geopolitical environmental and ethical challenges which is why recycling and diversification are major industry priorities q4 can cobalt be recycled from used batteries absolutely modern recycling processes can recover cobalt efficiently supporting supply security and sustainability q5 will cobalt still matter in future batteries likely yesespecially for highperformance applicationsthough its share may decline as alternative chemistries mature

learn from my mistake cold climate shoppers alright im here to confess how my arrogance is probably going to land me a 3000 cad repair bill on monday im not a car guy although i can do some basics im a lab tech i work with numbers a lot so when i needed a new suv i thought id really look into it make the best informed decision possible i didnt trust random reports on social media so i went to the biggest juiciest dataset i could online the usas nhtsa national highway traffic safety administration i took those reported issues weighed them based on severity summed it up divided it by the car sales and came up with my own little reliability index a little conditional formatting and the sheet was done and looking sexy the numbers seemed to make sense based on what id heard and lo and behold i found what i thought was a hidden deeply discounted gem the 2017 chevy equinox so i got one used 120 000 kms on it about 14 000 cad a joy to drive didnt have a single issue all summer all fall and all winter till now anyone who lives here knows that in ottawa weve been suffering an artic intrusion which basically means 15 degc 5 degf temperatures max for like 2 weeks last night i drove it a long while at 20 degc and it died on the highway barely made it to work had to get it towed to the mechanic after my shift google tells me that the cause is likely suffering from a failed positive crankcase ventilation pcv system which has caused excessive internal engine pressure leading to a blown rear main seal or other seal failure the combination of a lowpressure alarm burning smell and stalling at idlebut operating fine while movingis classic for this issue often triggered in cold weather google ai i now know that this is a common issue with this car the tow truck driver said he picked up like 14 equinoxes for the same thing this past week looking now its all over the internet and i thought to myself how did i not see this coming i used conditional formatting and everything but of course i trained the thing on usa data and unless youre alaskan you probably dont see temperatures like this very often so moral of the story if youre going to look online for recommendations for christs sake look for data from a country with a similar climate

econ five plan in depth the green economy the demand for electricity in china has grown rapidly matching its economic ascent the boom in data centers in recent years has only increased this appetite for power with more energy being added to the grid at an unprecedented rate at the same time the government has committed to a green transition with oil demand expected to peak by 2030 over the next five years the focus will be on the dual control of carbon aiming to manage both carbon intensity and total emissions to achieve these goals the government will expand existing emissions programs pursue new ambitious renewable energy projects and foster innovation in green technology fields emissions control starting with carbon emissions the existing ets program launched in 2021 will be expanded to cover heavy industries beginning with mining steel aluminium and cement this should increase the programs scope from 40 to 60 of total co emissions monitoring data from these newly included industries will be used to advance the program toward introducing emissions caps and tightening limits this will be accompanied by the gradual phasing in of permit auctioning shifting away from the current system of free permit allocations the ets will be accompanied by a revamped china certified emission reduction ccer program which will be boosted by the newly included ets industries the ccer program will increase its issuance of credits to meet the new demand these credits will also be aimed at financial institutions to encourage greater trading activity within the market renewable energy the chinese solar industry has become the worlds leading exporter of panels with the country leading in solar installations however there has been turbulence due to an oversupply of solar capacity and intense competition in the sector which has eroded profit margins to offset this the country has sought to increase solar exports to developing markets starting in 2026 the government will seek to taper off incentives and allow the industry to stabilize itself while prioritizing the stabilization of grid peaks through battery installations the mof has already announced the removal of export rebates for pv products for 2026 the vat export rebate rate for battery products will be reduced to 6 hydropower and wind projects have also expanded alongside solar in 2025 construction officially began on the medog hydropower station the project is set to exceed the three gorges dam as the worlds largest hydroelectric power station the aim is to add 15 terawatts of wind power domestically by 2030 while expanding wind exports abroad chinese wind companies are aiming to replicate their success in solar with new projects in europe and africa electric vehicles the chinese ev industry has been another major source of success within the green economy the ev market is highly competitive featuring advanced domestic automobiles evs have dominated new car purchases in the country reaching over 50 supported by state tradein subsidies these subsidies will remain in place for the next year currently ev exports have grown considerably with exports to emerging markets doubling strong sales in latin america southeast asia and other regions have helped offset tariffs and bans in european and north american markets the ministry of foreign affairs mofa will seek to reduce these trade restrictions on ev exports and introduce incentives to discourage new markets from imposing barriers such as in south africa through favorable trade agreements

i didnt believe the white deer rule until it followed me home i didnt tell anyone i was going that far in thats the part i keep circling back to like if i admit it out loud itll make sense why nobody came looking until the sun was already going down i just texted my brother heading up early back by afternoon no pin drop no ridge name no if i dont answer call someone id hunted these mountains since i was a kid i didnt think i needed the safety net and id heard the stories everyone around here has you grow up with them like you grow up with black ice and copperheadssomething you respect more than you believe dont whistle after dark dont follow a voice offtrail if you see a white deer you let it walk most people say that last one like a joke like theyre teasing you for being superstitious the old guys dont say it like a joke the old guys say it like theyre warning you about a sinkhole i went anyway it was the first sunday in december the kind of damp cold the appalachians do bestno movie snow just fog laid in the hollers and wet leaves that never fully dry i parked at a pulloff off forest service road 83 where the gravel was chewed up by trucks and the brown sign for the trailhead had a sticker slapped over it that said hell is real in block letters like somebody thought they were funny i threw my pack on checked my headlamp and stepped into the dark i carried a 308 id had since i was nineteen nothing fancy a rifle i trusted i had a small kitcat tourniquet a pack of quikclot gauze athletic tape a mylar blanket id never opened two game bags a cheap gps unit with a breadcrumb feature a knife id sharpened the night before while watching football i did everything right thats what makes it so hard to explain i was about two miles in when the world started to lighten the sky didnt turn pretty it just went from black to charcoal the ridge i was climbing ran like a spine steep on both sides the kind of place where your boots slide on dead leaves and you grab saplings to keep from skating downhill i moved slow on purpose i didnt want to sweat and freeze the woods had that quiet that isnt quiet owls further off a squirrel shaking a branch somewhere water moving over rock the kind of soundscape you stop noticing because its been your whole life then i saw it not right away not like it stepped out into a clearing it was a pale shape between two hemlocks halfhidden by mountain laurel at first i thought it was a fallen birch then it lifted its head and my brain made the jump a deer a buck white not kind of light or cream colored white like bone white like a sheet hung out to dry it stood still long enough for me to count the pointseight maybe tenand i felt that stupid sharp spike of adrenaline that hits a hunter when something rare walks into your sights i remember thinking is it legal not like id studied the regs for albino deer who does my mind did what minds do when they want something it grabbed for excuses a deer is a deer its not like im shooting an eagle i eased the rifle up rested against the trunk of an oak and looked through the scope the buck was facing slightly away head down picking at something under the leaves i could see the line of its back the shoulder the clean curve of its neck the shot was there i squeezed the recoil thumped into my shoulder the buck jolted kicked once and went down hard no sprint no crashing through brush just down i stood there for a second in that weird vacuum after a shot where youre listening for followup soundssomething bolting something dying out of sight there was nothing i walked up slow rifle still shouldered because habits keep you alive the fog was thicker down around where it fell cold moisture beaded on everythingmy sleeves the laurel leaves the bucks hideso when i got close its white coat looked already slick and darkened in patches like the woods were trying to claim it back before i even touched it i could smell the metallic edge of blood before i saw it it lay on its side like it had been placed there the eye facing up was open that eye is the thing i think about most it wasnt red like people always say with albinos it wasnt glowing it wasnt supernatural it was cloudy milky like cataracts the lashes were pale too almost invisible it made the buck look old sick wrong i knelt beside it and put my hand on its neck out of habit warmth was leaving fast the fur felt thin not sparse exactly just not as thick as youd expect in december i shouldve stopped right there i shouldve listened to that discomfort instead i did what i came to do i rolled it slightly and started field dressing you dont need the gore just know this when i opened it up the smell wasnt right not the normal warm musky gut smell this was sharp sour like ammonia like something had been fermenting inside it i paused knife in my hand and looked around the woods had gone silent not gradually not like its early and birds arent up it was like someone had turned down a dial no squirrel no water no little movement sounds just my breathing and the soft scrape of my glove against hide a branch snapped to my left not a small twig a branch heavy enough that it made that thick cracking sound i froze knife still in the deer i waited nothing moved no deer bounding away no bear huffing no human voice just fog hanging between trunks then it snapped again further back same direction like something taking a step and not caring if it made noise my heartbeat climbed and my brain did that dumb thing where it tries to be reasonable to keep you from panicking another hunter bear youre keyed up i pulled my knife out and stood rifle still slung i shouldered it thumbed off the safety and called out hey my voice didnt carry like it should have the fog swallowed it immediately no answer i looked down at the buck i looked at the open cavity and that wrong chemical stink i looked back at the trees i made a choice that felt stupid in the moment and feels even dumber now i decided to hurry finish what id started and get out i bent again working faster hands getting slick trying to keep my breathing steady thats when i cut myself ive dressed plenty of deer ive never cut myself doing it not like that my hand slipped and the knife edge slid across the heel of my palm not deep enough to hit anything major but enough that blood welled immediately warm and dark against my glove it stung in that clean sharp way that makes your stomach flip jesus i hissed clenching my hand as soon as my blood hit the leaves something in the woods answered a sound like a wet click not a bird call not a squirrel not a twig a wet deliberate click like someone tapping their tongue against the roof of their mouth it came from behind me i spun rifle up fog trunks laurel nothing thenanother click same sound closer my skin crawled every hair under my hat tried to stand up i started backing toward the ridge away from the deer and my boot slid on wet leaves i caught myself on a sapling and my injured hand smeared blood down the bark the sapling shook hard not from me from something else grabbing it i yanked my hand back and thats when i saw it not all of it just enough for my brain to latch onto the worst parts a shape behind the laurel tall and narrow too tall it wasnt a deer it wasnt a bear it was standing but it didnt stand like a person it leaned forward like it had forgotten what balance was and there was a smell rotten meat and something chemical underneath like bleach left too long in a closed room i raised my rifle and tried to find a clean line through the branches the shape shifted there was a pale flashbone hide i dont knowand then it was gone like it dropped out of view without making a crash the click sounded again this time off to my right like it had moved without moving i took
